package_info.package_versions: All versions after the S3 bucket was abandoned in mid-2023
package_info.why_malicious: After the S3 bucket used to host bignum's prebuilt binaries was abandoned, attackers took control of the bucket and replaced the legitimate binaries with malicious ones. As a result, any installation of the package fetched and executed attacker-supplied binaries, which exfiltrated sensitive user data.

execution_context.file_location: downloaded native binary from hijacked S3 bucket, referenced in package.json's install script
required_permissions: filesystem (to read credential and config files)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious native binary (replacing the original bignum binary) that, when executed during npm install, collects user credentials (such as environment variables, user IDs, passwords, and hostname) and exfiltrates them to an attacker-controlled S3 bucket.
malicious_snippets.code_language: native binary (platform-dependent, likely C/C++ or Node.js native addon)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the malicious binary executes as part of the package installation script, reads sensitive environment variables, user credentials, and hostname from the system, then sends this data via HTTP(S) to the attacker's S3 bucket, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The binary, executed during installation, accesses sensitive environment variables and credential files, then initiates outbound network connections to an untrusted S3 bucket. This behavior is highly anomalous for a math library and is indicative of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate bignum package should only provide mathematical operations and should not access user credentials, environment variables, or perform any network communication during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may collect anonymous telemetry with explicit user consent, but legitimate packages never access credentials or environment variables, nor do they exfiltrate sensitive data during install.
key_indicators: Replacement of official binary in remote storage without a corresponding package update
Install script or package.json referencing external S3 bucket for critical binaries
Binary accesses environment variables and credential files during install
Outbound network requests to attacker-controlled S3 bucket at install-time

attack_chain.action: Attacker identifies and claims the abandoned S3 bucket previously used by the bignum package to host its binaries.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control over the storage location for distributed binaries.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads a malicious binary to the same path as the original bignum binary in the S3 bucket.
attack_chain.leads_to: All future installations of the package will fetch the attacker's binary.

attack_chain.action: User installs or reinstalls the npm package, which fetches the binary from the hijacked S3 bucket as part of the install script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious binary is downloaded and executed on the user's system.

attack_chain.action: The malicious binary executes, harvesting credentials, environment variables, and system information, then exfiltrates this data to the attacker's S3 bucket.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive data from compromised systems.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of a downloaded native binary during npm package installation
Binary accesses environment variables and credential files (e.g., ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/)
Unexpected outbound network requests to S3 buckets during install-time
file_indicators: package.json or install scripts referencing external S3 buckets for binary downloads
Downloaded binaries with hashes that do not match known-good versions
Presence of native binaries in node_modules/bignum/bin/ with unexpected modification dates
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP(S) connections to S3 buckets not associated with the original bignum maintainers
Data exfiltration to S3 endpoints that were previously unused or newly registered
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for scripts that download and execute binaries from external sources, especially S3 buckets. Flag packages where install scripts reference external storage for critical binaries. Alert if binaries accessed during install attempt to read environment variables or credential files. Detect and block outbound network connections to S3 buckets not previously associated with the package or its maintainers, and verify binary hashes against trusted sources.
